summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: fluent in asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (sets, functions, modular arithmetic, primes and gcd, permutations, induction and recursion), first-course linear algebra (matrices, invertibility, rank, basis, dimension, linear maps over the rationals and the complex numbers), complex arithmetic with Euler's formula, and the basic Turing machine model with tapes and step counting. They have seen binary representation, bit operations such as XOR, and perhaps the idea of multiplying integers by divide and conquer, but have not been taught the discrete Fourier transform, the FFT, polynomial transforms, Schönhage–Strassen, abstract ring theory beyond the basic definition, tensor products, or numerical error analysis, and these are what the wiki must explain.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and residues
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers taken modulo a positive integer q, where Z/qZ denotes the residue classes 0,...,q-1 with addition and multiplication reduced mod q.

known.name: Primes, divisibility, gcd and coprimality
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1, and a residue is invertible modulo q exactly when it is coprime to q.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits with the leftmost bit most significant, padded on the left with zeros to a chosen length.

known.name: Bitwise XOR
known.gloss: The bit operation that outputs 1 exactly when its two inputs differ, equivalently addition modulo 2, and it is its own inverse.

known.name: Logarithms, floors, ceilings and powers of two
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm, floor and ceiling functions, and the exponent rules used to size parameters such as b = ceil(log2 n).

known.name: Matrices, invertibility and rank
known.gloss: Matrices act as linear maps on vectors, are composed by multiplication, are invertible when a two-sided inverse exists, and have a rank equal to the dimension of their image.

known.name: Vector spaces, basis and dimension
known.gloss: The first-course linear-algebra notions of a vector space over a field such as the rationals or complex numbers, its subspaces, bases and dimension, and linear combinations of vectors.

known.name: Permutations and permutation matrices
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite index set to itself, which reorders entries of an array and is represented by a matrix with exactly one 1 in each row and column.

known.name: Lexicographic order and index tuples
known.gloss: Tuples of indices are ordered by comparing the first entry, then the second, and so on, which matches how a multidimensional array is laid out in a flat sequence.

known.name: Euler's formula and roots of unity as points on the unit circle
known.gloss: e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta lies on the unit circle, so e^{2 pi i/q} is a q-th root of unity whose powers cycle with period q.

known.name: Geometric series and orthogonality of sums of roots of unity
aliases: sum of powers of a root of unity vanishes
known.gloss: The finite geometric series formula, and its consequence that the sum of all powers of a nontrivial q-th root of unity is zero while that of the trivial one is q.

known.name: Norms and the triangle inequality
known.gloss: A norm measures the size of a number or vector, obeys the triangle inequality, and is used to add up bounds on accumulated errors.

known.name: Rational numbers, dyadic rationals and exact arithmetic
known.gloss: Numbers of the form m/2^k with integer m, closed under addition and multiplication, and the idea that exact arithmetic on them is separate from rounding or truncating a real number.

known.name: Algebraic structures: groups, rings and isomorphisms
known.gloss: The basic definitions from a discrete-mathematics course of a set with operations satisfying axioms, and of a structure-preserving bijection between two such sets.

known.name: Discrete-math proof techniques
known.gloss: Proof by induction, recursive definitions and recurrences, and elementary counting, as used to bound the cost of a recursive procedure.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and divide-and-conquer multiplication
known.gloss: The standard O(n^2) digit-by-digit method for multiplying integers with carries, and the idea that splitting numbers into pieces can beat it.

known.name: Multitape machine cost model and linear-time scans
known.gloss: Time on a Turing machine counts head steps, so reading, copying or comparing a tape of N cells in order costs O(N), while random access to arbitrary cells costs more.

known.name: Complex polynomial evaluation and interpolation
known.gloss: A polynomial of degree below r is determined by its r coefficients or by its values at r distinct points, and these two representations are interchangeable.

known.name: Gaussian function
known.gloss: The function exp(-x^2), which decays rapidly away from zero and is used here as a smooth weight whose tails can be dropped with small error.

known.name: Convolution as polynomial multiplication
known.gloss: The convolution of two sequences has k-th entry equal to the sum of the products of entries whose indices add to k, which is exactly the coefficient list of the product of the corresponding polynomials.

known.name: Quantifiers, sets and basic asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: The notation Theta and Omega for tight and lower bounds, little-o for strictly smaller growth, and the distinction between worst-case upper bounds and lower bounds on an algorithm's running time.
